subject: Acme POC: evaluation plan, success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC: evaluation plan, success criteria & next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Recap + proposed next steps below (tl;dr at the top).

TL;DR: We (Redwood) will stand up a 2-week POC focused on customer-facing summarization; success = 3 KPIs (precision >= 85% on the rubric, median latency < 350ms, and acceptable hallucination rate < 5% on sample set). Draft eval plan attached.

Key items from the call:
- Scope: summarization for product release notes (structured input -> short summary).
- Users: 5 product managers + 2 support reps for feedback.
- Data: subset of anonymized release notes (we'll use the sample you shared).
- Success criteria (proposed):
  1) Accuracy/faithfulness: >=85% pass rate on our grading rubric (see attachment).
  2) Latency: 95th percentile < 400ms, median < 350ms with target request mix.
  3) Safety/hallucinations: <5% hallucination rate on blind eval set.
  4) Business acceptance: at least 4/5 average from product manager feedback.

Proposed POC timeline (2 weeks):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize eval plan, access + egress rules, and test data subset.
- Week 1: deploy model variant A (baseline) + run offline eval and limited online shadowing.
- Week 2: iterate based on results, run customer feedback sessions, finalize go/no-go decision.

Ownership:
- Redwood (Marissa): overall POC coordination, infra, and evaluation deliverables.
- Redwood (Dylan): runtime/config tuning, latency profiles, and batching plan.
- Acme (Alex/Priya): test-data prep, PM feedback sessions, and internal stakeholder sign-off.

Evals methodology question: we propose a hybrid approach — offline grading (human rubric) for fidelity + a 3-day online shadow run to validate production behavior and telemetry. Dylan / Neha, can you confirm the plan and whether we should expand the rubric to include style/conciseness metrics?

Attachments: Acme_POC_Eval_Plan_v1.xlsx (detailed tasks + metrics), ACME_POC_success_criteria.docx (rubric draft).

Next steps:
1) Alex: confirm access details and share sanitized sample by Wed 6/23.
2) Marissa/Dylan: finalize eval plan and send infra access form by Tue 6/22.
3) Schedule kickoff (30m) with PMs for Thu 6/24 — Alex to propose time.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0143
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC: evaluation plan, success criteria & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. Confirming a few items:

- Timeline & scope look good. Two quick clarifications: the PM feedback is aggregated (we'll give you anonymized scores + comments) and we may want to extend to 3 weeks if we need more iteration — can we flag that as an optional extension?
- I'll share a sanitized sample of release notes by EOD Wed 6/23. Priya will coordinate the PM availability for Thu 6/24.
- On the hybrid eval methodology: we prefer offline evals for fidelity but want a short 2-3 day online shadow to confirm latency at scale. The rubric looks fine, but can we add a 'domain-specific terminology' check (critical for our legal notices)?

Also looping in our security contact if we need specific egress controls — Priya, please advise.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Director, Product & Data, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC: evaluation plan, success criteria & next steps

Appreciate the quick confirmation, Alex — extension to 3 weeks is fine as an optional runway; we'll call it Week 3: iteration + follow-up. I'll update the plan.

On the rubric: adding a 'domain-specific terminology' axis makes sense. Proposal: scoring buckets for each example (0/1/2) where 2 = terminology correct and properly used, 1 = partially correct (minor issues), 0 = incorrect/missing. We'll add this to ACME_POC_success_criteria.docx and include examples.

Security/egress: Priya — if you can share the list of allowed endpoints and an S3 signed-url workflow for data transfer that works for you, we'll standardize the onboarding doc.

Dylan / Neha — action for you both:
- Dylan: can you draft the online shadow plan (traffic split, throttles, telemetry to capture — latency, token counts, error rates) by Tue 6/22 EOD?
- Neha: can you review the rubric and propose the offline grading instructions for human raters (blind labeling rules, consensus process, sample size) by Tue 6/22 EOD?

I'll also upload a first-pass of the eval tracking sheet to the Drive link and send an updated version of the attachments after edits.

—
Marissa
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC: evaluation plan, success criteria & next steps

Thanks — quick notes on the eval methodology from the grading side: 

1) Offline evals (human-in-the-loop):
- Sample size: 200 examples randomized from the sanitized set (stratified by doc length).
- Raters: 3 independent raters per example; use majority rule for pass/fail; tie -> adjudicator.
- Rubric axes: Factuality, Terminology, Conciseness, Tone/Style, Safety. Each axis scored 0/1/2 with guidance doc.
- Pass threshold: >=85% of examples must have average score >=1.5 across Factuality + Terminology.

2) Online shadowing:
- Short run (48–72 hours) routing 10% of live requests to Redwood sandbox (no public-facing responses). Capture production latency distribution, token counts, and any downstream errors.
- Telemetry: store request/response hashes, latency, token usage, and a hallucination flag from automated heuristics for spot checks.

Notes/questions:
- Need clarity on whether product managers will see de-anonymized outputs during feedback or only aggregated scores. Aggregated is preferable for privacy.
- For the human raters: recommend we blind-source system IDs and shuffle examples so raters don't see original ordering.

I'll put a short grading-instructions doc in Drive and link it here when ready.

-Neha
